text: dsh-service-hub 是面向 DSH 网页和桌面客户端的本机服务管理插件。它通过侧栏面板连接随插件启动的本地控制台，可登记并管理服务、一次性脚本和桌面应用，查看状态、日志与访问地址，并执行启动、停止或重启等操作。控制台使用本机 127.0.0.1:3999，注册表和日志保存在用户目录；不需要 API 密钥或外部账号。

dsh-service-hub adds a local service console to DSH web and desktop clients. The sidebar lists registered services, scripts, and apps so users can check status and logs or start and stop entries. It uses 127.0.0.1:3999 and stores registry data locally. No API key is required.
想在 DSH 侧栏集中查看和启停我登记的本机服务。
有没有办法从一个面板管理电脑上的脚本和应用？
I want a DSH sidebar to start and monitor my local services.
dsh-service-hub 的功能「本机服务控制台」：在侧栏打开本机控制台，查看登记项状态并进入管理界面；插件激活时启动控制台，面板提供刷新和浏览器打开入口。
dsh-service-hub 的功能「服务、脚本与应用管理」：控制台列出已登记的本机条目，并提供相应的启动、停止、重启和日志操作，方便从一处管理常用程序。

dsh-service-hub README · dsh-service-hub：[](https://dsh-plugin.org)

**Service Hub for DeepSeek Harness** — a sidebar panel that starts, stops, restarts and
monitors the local services, one-shot scripts and terminal tools you keep on your own
machine, so you no longer have to remember where each launcher lives.

dsh-service-hub README · Self-contained since 0.3.0：The package ships its own **zero-dependency console daemon** (`console/`, Node standard
library only). Installing the plugin is enough: the Host side starts the daemon on
`127.0.0.1:3999` when the plugin activates, and stops it when the plugin unloads.
No external tool, no machine-specific path, nothing to download.

Registry data and logs live in `~/.dsh-service-hub/`, so upgrading or reinstalling the
plugin keeps your service list.

dsh-service-hub README · What you get：The Harness sidebar gains a **Service** tab listing every registered entry with live
status, health, port and a quick access URL, plus **start / stop / restart / logs /
refresh** buttons and a LAN address you can open from a phone. Services you start keep
running when the panel is closed, because the daemon owns the process control.

dsh-service-hub README · Install：```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-service-hub
```

Then restart DeepSeek Harness (or reload the window) and open the **Service** tab.

From source before an npm release exists:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:liuhuan007/dsh-service-hub
```

dsh-service-hub README · Requirements：| Requirement | Why |
|---|---|
| DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1+ with the Web/Desktop UI | Client bundle targets `platform: web` |
| [`dsh-better-sidebar`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-better-sidebar) | The panel registers a sidebar tab through its service |
| Node 18+ | Runs the bundled console daemon (the desktop app ships one) |
| Windows | Process management uses PowerShell and `tasklist`/`netstat` |

dsh-service-hub README · Requirements：Port `3999` must be free. If another console already listens there, the plugin reuses it
instead of starting a second one.

dsh-service-hub README · Permissions and external services：- The client bundle only performs `fetch` against `http://127.0.0.1:3999` (localhost).
- The bundled daemon binds `127.0.0.1` only, never a public interface.
- No telemetry, no outbound network calls from the plugin itself.
- The daemon starts and stops processes that **you registered**; it does not run anything
  on its own. Each entry's command is visible in the panel and stored in
  `~/.dsh-service-hub/data/registry.json`.

dsh-service-hub README · Compatibility：- DSH: `>=0.2.1`
- UI: Web / Desktop (sidebar tab); no effect on the TUI or headless profiles
- OS: Windows

dsh-service-hub README · Known limitations：- The panel opens from the session header (⚙ 服务). Installing `dsh-better-sidebar` additionally adds the same panel as a left sidebar tab; it is optional.
- Panel text is currently Chinese only; `locale/` ships `meta.title` /
  `meta.description` in English and Chinese for the plugin inventory.
- Console URL is fixed to `127.0.0.1:3999`.

dsh-service-hub README · Discovery tries to classify each candidate：`Scan` lists unregistered executables and listening ports. Every candidate carries a
suggested kind before you add it — `app` for install-directory programs and shortcuts,
`service` for programs that listen on a port, `terminal` for command wrappers in npm or
user bin directories, `script` for other batch files — and the discovery dialog shows a
kind selector, so the guess is always overridable. System directories (`C:\Windows\...`)
are skipped.
section: Discovery tries to classify each candidate

text: dsh-service-hub README · Security：The bundled console listens on `127.0.0.1` only and is guarded against drive-by use:

dsh-service-hub README · Security：- **No CORS headers.** Browser requests from any other origin fail at preflight, so a
  random website cannot read `/api/state` or call mutating endpoints.
- **Origin / Sec-Fetch / Host guard.** Script-initiated cross-site requests get `403`;
  top-level and iframe navigation stays allowed so the panel can embed the page.
- **Safe ids.** Entry ids are limited to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}` and every log path is
  resolved inside the log directory, so `/api/items/<id>/logs` cannot read other files.
- **`/healthz`** exposes only `{ ok, version, pid }` plus the `X-LC-Daemon` header, which
  the Host uses to confirm it is talking to this plugin's daemon and not an unrelated
  process that happens to occupy port 3999.

dsh-service-hub README · Security：The daemon can start and stop the commands **you registered**; it never runs anything on
its own. Run `npm test` to see the regression suite for these guarantees.

dsh-service-hub README · Layout：The console is this plugin. There is no separate project to install or keep in sync:

```
lib/            Host plugin (auto-starts the console) and the sidebar client bundle
console/        The console daemon + single-page UI, shipped as part of the package
scripts/        Developer helpers (start-console.cmd for manual debugging)
locale/, icon.svg, cordis.patch.yml

dsh-service-hub README · Layout：Data and logs live in `~/.dsh-service-hub/`, so the console, the sidebar panel and a
manually started instance all read the same registry.

dsh-service-hub README · Development：```bash
npm test              # security + API regression tests (node:test)
npm pack --dry-run    # inspect the published file list
```
